trust_decision.summary: Each list service decides which HTTP query-string keys become SQL column identifiers, interpolated raw into TypeORM andWhere(`<alias>.${key} LIKE :${key}`); at the pinned commit there is no decision at all (every leftover key is trusted). The fix adds a per-entity column allow-list.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'dynamic column names in TypeORM query builders'; article is the main public list (GET /article) and the first service with the `${key}` interpolation.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: server/src/modules/article/article.controller.ts:64-71 (headless API-key route spreads the raw query into articleService.findAll with status forced; it is covered automatically by the service-level fix and is only out of scope if a solver fixes in the GET /article controller)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The uncovered list services (view, search, smtp, user) sit behind JwtAuthGuard or admin role, so a solver can argue 'only the unauthenticated public lists are attacker-reachable'; but POST /user/register is open, so any registered user reaches view/search/smtp.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Admin list pages filter by arbitrary real columns via query keys (file by originalname, comment/user by email, article by title); dropping all extra query keys, or allow-listing too narrowly, breaks these LIKE filters.

O6_input_shapes: arbitrary query-string key used as a column identifier (exact-match allow-list, fix.diff:397-401)
reserved keys page/pageSize/status/pass removed before the allow-list (fix.diff:394)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /api/view: view.service findAll interpolates every leftover query key as a column (JwtAuthGuard only, no role)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: authenticated-only analytics list, not a public endpoint

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /api/search: search.service findAll same interpolation (JwtAuthGuard only)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: authenticated-only search-history list; the public search path (searchArticle) is parameterised

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /api/smtp: smtp.service findAll same interpolation (JwtAuthGuard only)
GET /api/user: user.service findAll same interpolation (admin role)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: tag findAll gaining the same `${key} LIKE` filter loop over leftover query params
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every other list service in the repo already copies this exact loop; tag/category lists take @Query() params (server/src/modules/tag/tag.controller.ts:31-32).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an orderBy(`article.${sortField}`, order) sort parameter on category/tag article lists
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Admin tables sort by column; a maintainer would add a sort key next to the existing hard-coded orderBy, and an allow-list scoped to WHERE keys would not cover it (how-type: identifier in ORDER BY, not WHERE).

O9_family: SQL injection via unvalidated identifier (column name) in an ORM query builder

O10_build.toolchain: Node >=16.5, pnpm workspace (depends on @fecommunity/reactpress-toolkit workspace:*), NestJS 6, TypeORM 0.2.45, jest 24 + ts-jest
services: MySQL (mysql2) for end-to-end; unit tests can mock the repository/query builder
O10_build.project_tests: None for the server: no *.spec.ts under server/src and no server/test directory despite the jest config at server/package.json:136-149; only cli/tests exist.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a column allow-list to the five public list services only (or only article), leaving view/search/smtp/user with the identical loop because they need auth.

out_of_scope_notes: The same fix commit also adds JwtAuthGuard to POST /comment and an HTML sanitiser for comment html (fix.diff:51, fix.diff:73); that is a separate XSS change, not CWE-89.
The published article allow-list includes 'password' (fix.diff:351), which keeps a LIKE-based oracle on article passwords through the public list; this is a separate information-exposure issue.

Weakness for task difficulty: all 9 sinks share a byte-identical line (`LIKE :${key}`), so one grep finds every uncovered route. Per lessons-v2 these are WHERE-type siblings of one concept and will likely fall together, and the real code offers little how-type room.
